title: A Simple, Interpretable Machine Learning Model Based on Clinical Factors Accurately Predicts Incident Dysplasia or Malignancy in Barrett's Esophagus.
summary: A decision tree trained on a retrospective Barrett esophagus cohort identified segment length alone as a useful risk-stratification predictor for observed progression. In 598 patients (61 progressors), the held-out test set achieved AUROC .79; lowering the threshold raised sensitivity to 93.3% with specificity 58.5%. This is single-center retrospective evidence and is not an externally validated surveillance recommendation.
ai_technology: Supervised decision tree among six ML classifiers uses five candidate predictors; the selected tree relies only on Barrett segment length.
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: In 598 patients with follow-up through Jan 2024, 61 progressed within five years. The tree’s held-out test AUROC was .79; default sensitivity/specificity were 73.3%/70.4%, and a lower threshold yielded 93.3% sensitivity/58.5% specificity; segment-length thresholds define four risk groups.
evidence.unknown: The model was developed on 75% of a single-center veteran cohort and tested on a 25% held-out split (n=150); progressor pathology was independently verified by a second expert pathologist. No external cohort was used, calibration was suboptimal, and the sensitivity threshold trades specificity for fewer false negatives.
